Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "Gulliver's Travels", "unit": 13, "heading": "CHAPTER I.", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en99-013-0013", "target": "Помню, когда я был в Лилипутии, цвет лица этих малорослых людей казался мне прекраснейшим на свете; и, беседуя об этом с одним тамошним учёным, моим близким другом, я услышал от него, что моё лицо казалось ему гораздо белее и глаже, когда он смотрел на меня с земли, чем при более близком рассмотрении, когда я брал его на руку и подносил к самому лицу, что, как он признался, было поначалу весьма поразительным зрелищем. Он сказал, что «он видит на моей коже большие ямы; что щетина моей бороды в десять раз крепче кабаньей и что цвет моего лица составлен из нескольких цветов, совершенно неприятных», хотя я должен просить позволения сказать в своё оправдание, что я так же бел, как большинство людей моего пола и страны, и очень мало загорел за все мои путешествия. С другой стороны, рассуждая о дамах при дворе того императора, он имел обыкновение говорить мне: «у одной веснушки; у другой слишком большой рот; у третьей слишком большой нос», — ничего из чего я не мог различить. Признаю, что это размышление довольно очевидно; тем не менее я не мог его удержать, чтобы читатель не подумал, будто эти огромные существа в самом деле уродливы: ибо я должен отдать им справедливость и сказать, что это красивый народ, и в особенности черты лица моего хозяина, хотя он был всего лишь фермер, когда я смотрел на него с высоты шестидесяти футов, казались вполне соразмерными.", "source_sha256": "952fd292d1b99b673125b32aa67f92b7ab8fd83cd7354d73d7ee3be2a6c72d04", "target_id": "ru-en99-013-0013", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "82ba7b254029757c664f7bddfc37ac58abd72eb3f17fa5e2d6d221307dffe457"}, {"source_id": "en99-013-0014", "target": "Когда обед кончился, мой хозяин пошёл к своим работникам и, как я мог понять по его голосу и жестам, строго наказал жене заботиться обо мне. Я очень устал и склонялся ко сну, что хозяйка заметила: она положила меня на собственную постель и накрыла чистым белым платком, но большим и грубее, чем грот военного корабля.", "source_sha256": "18642b90a3376b4bccfbe16479348aaae069992b834a015980b19aa003fd04c3", "target_id": "ru-en99-013-0014", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "75e4a6818facd6274e9bf8be5e689d6cdb25a4807db02ac0c117b8d458683129"}], "source_language": "English", "part": 2, "book": null, "chapter": 1, "role": "PRINCIPAL_CHAPTER"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en99-013-0015", "tag": "p", "text": "I slept about two hours, and dreamt I was at home with my wife and children, which aggravated my sorrows when I awaked, and found myself alone in a vast room, between two and three hundred feet wide, and above two hundred high, lying in a bed twenty yards wide. My mistress was gone about her household affairs, and had locked me in. The bed was eight yards from the floor. Some natural necessities required me to get down; I durst not presume to call; and if I had, it would have been in vain, with such a voice as mine, at so great a distance from the room where I lay to the kitchen where the family kept. While I was under these circumstances, two rats crept up the curtains, and ran smelling backwards and forwards on the bed. One of them came up almost to my face, whereupon I rose in a fright, and drew out my hanger to defend myself. These horrible animals had the boldness to attack me on both sides, and one of them held his forefeet at my collar; but I had the good fortune to rip up his belly before he could do me any mischief. He fell down at my feet; and the other, seeing the fate of his comrade, made his escape, but not without one good wound on the back, which I gave him as he fled, and made the blood run trickling from him. After this exploit, I walked gently to and fro on the bed, to recover my breath and loss of spirits. These creatures were of the size of a large mastiff, but infinitely more nimble and fierce; so that if I had taken off my belt before I went to sleep, I must have infallibly been torn to pieces and devoured. I measured the tail of the dead rat, and found it to be two yards long, wanting an inch; but it went against my stomach to drag the carcass off the bed, where it lay still bleeding; I observed it had yet some life, but with a strong slash across the neck, I thoroughly despatched it.", "sha256": "883cfadc5e0ec74c0efe9d40d6416dcc3e4a7c1cbe7cd71937c01e399a58eab8", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[15]/p[15]", "source_html_sha256": "dde24521e699986dbb25caea7144e993584495a35ad077d86027c42ee42e943c", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-013-0016", "tag": "p", "text": "Soon after my mistress came into the room, who seeing me all bloody, ran and took me up in her hand. I pointed to the dead rat, smiling, and making other signs to show I was not hurt; whereat she was extremely rejoiced, calling the maid to take up the dead rat with a pair of tongs, and throw it out of the window. Then she set me on a table, where I showed her my hanger all bloody, and wiping it on the lappet of my coat, returned it to the scabbard. I was pressed to do more than one thing which another could not do for me, and therefore endeavoured to make my mistress understand, that I desired to be set down on the floor; which after she had done, my bashfulness would not suffer me to express myself farther, than by pointing to the door, and bowing several times. The good woman, with much difficulty, at last perceived what I would be at, and taking me up again in her hand, walked into the garden, where she set me down. I went on one side about two hundred yards, and beckoning to her not to look or to follow me, I hid myself between two leaves of sorrel, and there discharged the necessities of nature.", "sha256": "105ba57df4e8f24bc3f50950cd90daa98681546ea7f0b1f620d90b91d8110b46", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[15]/p[16]", "source_html_sha256": "18633e85428eca8a818db6b8b2e38138a21cc00c0c46fe9d158159ac5eac82f8", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}, {"id": "en99-013-0017", "tag": "p", "text": "I hope the gentle reader will excuse me for dwelling on these and the like particulars, which, however insignificant they may appear to groveling vulgar minds, yet will certainly help a philosopher to enlarge his thoughts and imagination, and apply them to the benefit of public as well as private life, which was my sole design in presenting this and other accounts of my travels to the world; wherein I have been chiefly studious of truth, without affecting any ornaments of learning or of style. But the whole scene of this voyage made so strong an impression on my mind, and is so deeply fixed in my memory, that, in committing it to paper I did not omit one material circumstance: however, upon a strict review, I blotted out several passages of less moment which were in my first copy, for fear of being censured as tedious and trifling, whereof travellers are often, perhaps not without justice, accused.", "sha256": "419b9c69a1a8fde78fc06ff861678b8877b6f4cd3a23c7e9ffb10e45bd9fc256", "role": "paragraph", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[15]/p[17]", "source_html_sha256": "e18fb4e32325673c1edd1ff6454d1b72d38b171aa64ce4b2b1104e5770140524", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "br_count": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": null, "source_container_role": null}]}
